issues.description: The delimiter argument complects two concepts: a literal character and an OpenAPI style name
issues.detail: The _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict maps both ',' and 'spaceDelimited' through one parameter. These are two different kinds of values — a character and a symbolic style identifier — sharing one string-typed slot. A caller passing user input could surprise the API. Simpler: accept only characters; expose the OAS constants as named module attributes the caller resolves explicitly.

issues.description: EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: feature is layered on top of auto_parse_qs_csv instead of decomposing the splitting concern
issues.detail: There are now three overlapping ways a query value becomes a list: multi-instance, auto_parse_qs_csv at parse time, and post-hoc delimiter splitting at read time. The docstring spends paragraphs explaining the interactions. The essential operation — split a string by a delimiter — is trivial; the complication is the surrounding policy lattice. The question that should have been asked first: should splitting be a parser-level value transformation rather than a per-call read-time concern?

issues.description: Raising ValueError for unsupported delimiter conflates argument validation with request data errors
issues.detail: get_param_as_list documents that ValueError from transforms becomes HTTPBadRequest. A programmer-error 'unsupported delimiter' now flows through the same channel as a malformed client value. These are different concerns — programmer mistake vs. bad client input — and they should not share an exception type at this boundary. Consider TypeError or a dedicated ConfigurationError.

issues.description: Identity dict _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS contains redundant self-mappings of single characters
issues.detail: Three of the five entries map a character to itself. The data structure is doing two jobs: validating membership and translating style names to characters. A frozenset of supported characters plus a small dict for the two style aliases would say more clearly what each piece means. Small thing, but the current shape hides which entries are aliases.

review.summary: The feature itself is small and the implementation is direct, but it sits on top of an already-complected splitting story (multi-instance values, auto_parse_qs_csv, and now per-call delimiter) and the docstring's three paragraphs of interaction notes are evidence of that. The delimiter argument also complects two distinct concepts — a literal character and an OpenAPI style name — behind one string parameter and one lookup table. None of this is a blocker; the code works and the tests exercise the real cases. The hammock question worth asking before merge: is splitting a read-time policy or a parser-time value transformation, and if the latter, would this live more simply alongside auto_parse_qs_csv as a configurable delimiter set?
